key_insight: SciML can replace expensive full-order fluid-transport simulations with fast surrogates by combining physics constraints, reduced-order models, and nonlinear latent-space learning.
engineering_relevance: These methods can accelerate prediction for coupled flow-transport problems such as turbidity currents and thermal convection, reducing computational cost while preserving key dynamics.
method: SVD-based reduced-order modeling, including Dynamic Mode Decomposition
Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) for governing-equation-constrained surrogates
β-Variational Autoencoders (β-VAEs) to extract disentangled nonlinear flow modes
evidence_signal: The chapter surveys and extends methods on representative benchmark problems such as lock-exchange flows, turbidity currents, and Rayleigh-Bénard convection, emphasizing accuracy-versus-cost tradeoffs.
watch_item: Performance is problem-dependent, and gains in speed or generalization may be limited by data regime, strong nonlinearity, and the assumptions built into the surrogate.
paper_title: Advances in Scientific Machine Learning for Coupled Fluid Flow and Transport
